subject: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novalytics.com>, Tom Baker <tbaker@novalytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call, I put three structurally different options below that should cover the procurement/finance scenarios you described. The attached PDF is a redlineable proposal (Novalytics_MA-Proposal_v2.pdf) and I included a quick usage extract (usage_breakdown_Q4.csv) to anchor the ramp figures.

High-level options (select one to move forward):

1) Multi-year ramp (preferred economics)
   - 3-year term, committed baseline ramps: year1 = 35% baseline, year2 = +40% add, year3 = +25% add
   - Annual invoicing for committed baseline; overages billed monthly at unit rates in attachment
   - 12% price protection vs public list for the term; option to buy extra capacity at fixed unit price

2) Short-term co-term with true-up
   - 12-month co-term aligning to Mar 31 billing cycle
   - Quarterly true-ups; baseline set at current Q4 run rate; overages billed monthly
   - Lower upfront commitment, higher unit price vs option 1

3) Annual auto-renew (flex-first)
   - 12 month recurring period with automatic renewal unless 30d notice
   - Quarterly capacity windows (0/25/50/75/100% increases) allowed with 45d notice; price for increments fixed for quarter

Please review and tell me which direction you'd prefer and any constraints from finance (PO timing, invoice recipient, procurement playbook). If helpful I can turn option 1 into a 2-year variant — Rafael and I discussed a middle-ground.

Attachments: Novalytics_MA-Proposal_v2.pdf, usage_breakdown_Q4.csv

Next steps: pick option + confirm PO timeline and any required contract language (auto-renew opt-out window, capacity spike protection).

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tbaker@novalytics.com>
Date: 2027-01-19T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal

Hi Irene —

Thanks for laying these out, very helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement/finance before we can commit: 

- Billing cadence: for option 1, can we get annual invoicing for the committed baseline but have overages billed quarterly (instead of monthly)? That helps our forecasting.
- Ramp ceiling: we need a hard cap on year-over-year committed growth unless we approve in writing. Can you confirm a max of +30% YoY baseline increase for the ramp and a mechanism to handle unexpected spikes (e.g., burst buffer with 72-hour throttled routing vs immediate overage charges)?
- SOC 2 evidence: procurement needs the latest SOC 2 type II report and data retention policy; can you attach those or point me to a secure link?
- PO process: finance@novalytics.com is the invoice recipient; procurement@novalytics.com will issue the PO. I attached our checklist (Novalytics_RFP_ProcurementChecklist.pdf).

If you can answer the bullets above and send a clean track-changes proposal, we can route internally and aim to return a PO within 10 business days.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Elena Garcia
VP, Platform Engineering | Novalytics
elena.garcia@novalytics.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-19T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal

Irene / Karthik —

Thanks — looping in a proposed compromise we can present that typically passes procurement while keeping unit economics acceptable:

Proposal (internal suggestion):
- 2-year term (trading a little term for acquisition risk):
  Year 1 committed baseline = 40% above current Q4 run-rate
  Year 2 committed baseline increase = +60% vs current Q4 (final baseline = year1 +60%)
- Billing: annual invoice for committed baseline (net 30); overages aggregated monthly but invoiced quarterly (gives Novalytics forecasting runway)
- Overage pricing: fixed unit price as in the v2 proposal; add-on capacity can be purchased at a 7% premium above committed unit rate for immediate delivery
- Ramp protection: hard cap on YoY committed uplift settable at +30% by default; any request above cap requires a signed amendment and 45d lead time

Quick numbers (illustrative):
- Current Q4 run-rate baseline: 100k tokens/day
- Year1 committed baseline: 140k tokens/day
- Year2 committed baseline: ~224k tokens/day (40% then +60%)

This keeps the customer in a committed cadence (better unit economics) while giving them quarterly visibility and a predictable invoicing cadence. If procurement insists on co-terming to Mar 31, we can phase the first invoice amount pro rata.

Irene — if we agree, I can draft the contract language for the ramp cap and billing cadence. Karthik — any immediate legal flags?

— Rafael
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-19T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal

Quick legal/procurement notes —

- Auto-renew: acceptable with a 30-day opt-out window prior to renewal; include an annual notice to customer 60 days ahead of renewal date.
- Capacity changes: mid-term committed baseline increases should require 45-day notice and will be subject to a price adjustment; provide a capped emergency burst plan (48-72h) with predefined throttling and an emergency rate (higher) to avoid surprise billing disputes.
- SLA/Credits: ensure SLA language and credits are in the SOW; any material latency or availability issues should map to credits only against committed baseline, not overages.

Rafael — the 2-year approach is fine; we should mark clause options in the contract so Novalytics can initial. I can provide redline suggestions today if you want to present the 2-year option.

Karthik
Sr. Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit phasing & annualization options for Novalytics renewal

Irene / Rafael / Karthik —

Thanks — we discussed internally and Novalytics is comfortable moving forward on the 2-year phased commit you proposed with these final items confirmed: 

- 2-year term; Year1 baseline 40% above Q4 run-rate, Year2 +60% as outlined.
- Annual billing for committed baseline (net 30), overages aggregated monthly and invoiced quarterly.
- Ramp protection: default hard cap at +30% YoY unless both parties sign an amendment.
- Emergency burst: allowable 72h buffer with throttling; emergency rate applies beyond buffer.
- 6-month review clause to evaluate actual usage vs committed baseline and make any mutually agreed adjustments.

Procurement will issue a PO within 7 business days to procurement@novalytics.com; finance will accept invoices at finance@novalytics.com. I attached a signed intent (Novalytics_PO_Intent.pdf) to advance contracting.

Please send a final, clean agreement with the clauses above and a DocuSign link and we'll execute.

Elena
VP, Platform Engineering | Novalytics
